discovery: Theoretical prediction and identification of neutron-star mergers as a site of rapid neutron-capture (r-process) nucleosynthesis through kilonova emission

nominees.name: Brian D. Metzger
nominees.affiliation: Columbia University and Flatiron Institute, USA

nominees.name: Daniel Kasen
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Berkeley and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, USA

nominees.name: Tsvi Piran
nominees.affiliation: The Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Israel

motivation: Where the elements heavier than iron were made has been one of the great open questions of physics since 1957. Piran and collaborators proposed in 1989 that neutron-star mergers eject neutron-rich matter where the r-process operates. Metzger and co-workers predicted in 2010 that radioactive decay of freshly synthesised r-process nuclei would power a distinct transient, the kilonova. Kasen's radiative-transfer calculations showed that lanthanide opacities make this emission red and long-lived. These predictions were confirmed in detail by AT2017gfo following GW170817, the first direct observation of heavy-element nucleosynthesis in the cosmos. Their work turned a qualitative idea into a quantitative, testable framework that now links laboratory measurements of exotic-nucleus masses, half-lives and fission properties directly to astronomical light curves and spectra, and it defines the programme of radioactive-beam facilities worldwide.
